terra.problem: The joke compares a person hoping not to be called on at a meeting to a fool, making that person the target of a joke about intelligence.
Not opening his mouth does not establish that the fool has nothing to say. The verse also does not show whether a loud voice indicates wisdom.
The claim that nobody can hide behind not knowing goes beyond the text's questions about the One who weighs hearts and guards life.
The explanation says the righteous man falls seven times as a certainty. The verse says that though he may fall seven times, he still gets up.
Getting up is presented as the opposite of giving up hope, but the verse does not describe the righteous man's feelings. The promise about finding wisdom does not establish them either.
Saying that getting back up sets the righteous apart implies that the wicked do not get back up. The verse says they stumble but does not say what happens afterward.
The explanation presents the wicked stumbling in bad times as the teacher's stated reason not to envy them. The passage does not make that connection.
The nap punchline does not have a clear connection to the verse's statement about having no future.
Sudden destruction does not establish that there will be no warning.
The explanation identifies the rebellious as the ones who bring destruction, but the BSB says only 'they' and leaves that identification open.
